mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-rate hike periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20-day forward window after triggering events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% suggests accelerating demand growth, which lowers real interest rates implicitly and supports equity price appreciation in the near term.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under the signal are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -1% indicates weakening supply-side conditions, which can trigger risk-off flows and depress S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite the supply shock (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, it indicates a shift toward accommodative policy, which historically precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return in non-recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative during the post-crossing period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of accelerating inflation (implied by a rising CPIAUCSL trend), the Fed tends to raise rates, which reduces the present value of equities, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during stable inflation periods (p > 0.05).
